newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end steady in thin trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Monday in thin trade with the absence of major offtake depressing sentiment in the local exchange, dealers said.
"Nothing much happened. It's still very thin and quiet. There were no inquiries and no buyers. What else is there to do?" a rubber trader in a foreign commodity house said.
Dealers said there was no spillover buying which could buoy the market the way it did last Friday, when covering for RSS3 rubber saw the volume rise to 10,895 tonnes.
The trade was also skeptical about whether the Thai government will intervene in the market.
"I have my doubts about that," a trader said, refering to reports Bangkok will come in by raising the price level at which it intervenes to 27 baht from 25 baht a kg.
Total volume traded for the day reached around 900 tonnes, sharply down from the 13,905 tonnes traded last Friday.

At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen unchanged at 122.00 U.S. cents a kg. April RSS1 was seen at 171.00-173.00 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.22) a kg from the previous 173.25 cents. April TSR20 was seen at 168.50-170.50 Singapore cents (US$1.18-$1.20) a kg from 168.50 cents.
